To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
context-sensitive-chunk approach to BPTT-based training of deep LSTM/BLSTMs is effective in reducing long-range language-model effect and improving handwriting recognition performance.
context-sensitive-chunk-based training and recognition is a promising approach to training and deploying deep LSTM and BLSTM for handwriting recognition.

(1) a context-sensitive-chunks based approach to BPTT training is proposed for deep (B)LSTM RNNs for online handwriting recognition, (2) it brings following benefits: reduced effect of long-range dependencies, more efficient mini-batch based BPTT training on GPU, and lower latency recognition with short context-sensitive-chunk size, (3) it is evaluated on IAM benchmark and performs better than previous state-of-the-arts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three aspects: (1) a new BPTT training approach for deep (B)LSTM RNNs, which splits each sequence into chunks with contextual information appended; (2) an efficient implementation of this approach on GPU, using mini-batch training and data-parallel training; (3) a low-latency handwriting recognition system, using a (B)LSTM with chunk-based context sensitive training and recognition.
the following two aspects: (1) how to make the (B)LSTM-based handwriting recognition more efficient and (2) how to make it more accurate.

the following three issues: (1) a novel context-sensitive-chunk-based BPTT training algorithm for deep (B)LSTM RNNs; (2) the design of a new character-level deep BLSTM RNN for online handwriting recognition; (3) the development of a novel low-latency online handwriting recognition system using deep BLSTM Rnn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach achieves the best results on the IAM dataset to the best of our knowledge.
our proposed context-sensitive-chunk approach to training deep BLSTM RNN is an important step forward for the development of low-latency handwriting recognition systems.

we have proposed and implemented a context-sensitive-chunks based BPTT approach for training deep (B)LSTM RNNs for offline handwriting recognition that brings the benefits of (a) better recognition accuracy than previous state-of-the art BPTT approaches, (b) low-latency recognition, and (c) more efficient training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose to train (B)LSTM RNNs using context-sensitive-chunk-based BPTT approach, and this approach can be used to train deep (B)LSTM with more hidden layers for better recognition accuracy, and it can also be used to train a deep (B)LSTMs with fewer layers to achieve a low-latency handwriting recognition system.
the context-sensitive-chunk approach to BPTT training for (B)LSTM RNN can bring benefits to both training and recognition.
our context-sensitive-chunk approach is an effective and efficient training method for deep LSTM and BLSTM RNNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BPTT-based approach to training deep recurrent neural networks can be made more effective by splitting each training sequence into context-sensitive chunks.
a context-sensitive chunk BPTT approach is a promising alternative to the conventional sentence-based BPTT approach for training deep (B)LSTM RNNs.
a simple and effective approach to training deep RNNs for offline handwriting recognition can be achieved by splitting the training sequences into chunks with appended short context information.
